title: Pointwise nonemptiness of a fibre product over an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $C$ and $U$ be schemes over $S$ with morphisms $c:C\to E$ and $u:U\to E$. If points $x\in|C|$ and $y\in|U|$ have the same image in the point set $|E|$ of the algebraic space, the set of field-valued point classes of [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] (equivalently, their maps from spectra of fields [def-weil-field] become equal after a common field extension), then the sheaf fibre product $C\times_EU$, which is represented by a scheme, has a point whose projections map to $x$ and $y$ (after that common field extension). In particular, if every point of $c(C)$ lies in the image of $u$, then the projection $C\times_EU\to C$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Tag 03H4 (spaces-properties, lemma-points-cartesian), the pointwise fibre-product criterion for an algebraic space; the equivalent common-field formulation is part of the definition of points of an algebraic space.

proof.text: The scheme product $C\times_SU$ exists by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The diagonal of $E$ is representable by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Pulling this diagonal back along the map $C\times_SU\to E\times_SE$ induced by $c$ and $u$ therefore gives a scheme representing compatible pairs of maps to $C$ and $U$ with equal composites to $E$. This representing scheme is the sheaf fibre product $C\times_EU$, with its two projection morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), together with the representability-of-the-diagonal definition in Tag 025Y

proof.text: Choose representatives $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to C$ and $b:\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$ for $x$ and $y$, with $K$ and $L$ fields [def-weil-field]. Equality of their images in $|E|$ means, by the common-field point-class relation [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family], that there are a field $M$ and embeddings $K\to M$, $L\to M$ for which the two composites to $E$ agree. The resulting compatible pair gives, by the representing property in Step 1, a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}M\to C\times_EU$ whose projections are the restrictions of $a$ and $b$; hence those projections represent $x$ and $y$. If every point of $c(C)$ lies in the image of $u$, apply this construction to each point $x$ of $C$ and a point $y$ lying over the same point of $E$. The projection then hits every underlying point of $C$, which is exactly surjectivity of a scheme morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism].
